<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="Section16abeneficialOwnershipRepo_071305"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Section&nbsp;16(a)&nbsp;Beneficial
Ownership Reporting Compliance</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Section&nbsp;16(a)&nbsp;of
the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 requires InfraSource Services&#146; directors,
executive officers (including persons performing a principal policy-making
function), and persons who own more than 10% of a registered class of
InfraSource Services&#146;s equity securities (&#147;10% Holders&#148;) to file with the SEC
initial reports of ownership and reports of changes in ownership of our common
stock. Directors, officers and 10% Holders are required by the regulations
under the Exchange Act to file all Section&nbsp;16(a)&nbsp;reports
electronically and to provide us with notice of all Section&nbsp;16(a)&nbsp;reports
which they file. Based solely upon a review of the Section&nbsp;16(a)&nbsp;reports
filed electronically by such reporting persons, and the representations made by
the reporting persons to us, we believe that during the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2005, our directors, officers and 10% Holders complied with the filing
requirements under Section&nbsp;16(a)&nbsp;of the Exchange Act.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="CodeOfBusinessConductAndEthics_071358"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Code of Business Conduct and Ethics</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have a Code of Business Conduct and Ethics, which
is applicable to all of our employees. For purposes of Section&nbsp;406 of the
Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 and the related SEC rules, the sections of the Code
of Business Conduct and Ethics entitled &#147;General Policy: Compliance with Laws,&#148;
&#147;Conflicts of Interest,&#148; &#147;Securities Laws and Insider Trading,&#148; &#147;Reporting any
Illegal or Unethical Behavior,&#148; and &#147;Compliance Procedures&#148; constitute the
Company&#146;s Code of Ethics for Principal Executives and Senior Financial
Officers, including the Company&#146;s Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial
Officer, and Chief Accounting Officer or Controller (or person performing
similar function).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Code of Business
Conduct and Ethics is designed to deter wrongdoing and promote ethical conduct,
full and accurate reporting in our SEC filings, compliance with applicable law,
as well as other matters. The Code of Business Conduct and Ethics is posted on
our website (<i><font style="font-style:italic;">www.infrasourceinc.com</font></i>).</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="CorporateGovernance_071414"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Corporate Governance</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 11.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our Board of Directors
believes that the purpose of corporate governance is to ensure that stockholder
value is maximized in a manner consistent with the strategic plans of our
company, legal requirements, the highest standards of integrity and other
standards. Our Board adheres to corporate governance practices that the Board
and senior management believe promote this purpose and are sound. It is our
practice to review these governance practices, Delaware law (the state in which
InfraSource Services is incorporated), the Corporate Governance Listing
Standards of the New York Stock Exchange (the &#147;NYSE Standards&#148;), and the
regulations of the U.S.&nbsp;Securities and Exchange Commission (the &#147;SEC&#148;), as
well as best practices suggested by recognized governance authorities from time
to time, as needed.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="AuditCommittee_071416"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Audit Committee</font></b></p>

2006, our Audit Committee consists of Richard Siudek (Chairman), J.&nbsp;Michal
Conaway and David H. Watts. During the fiscal year ended December&nbsp;31,
2005, and until he was replaced </font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(1)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>For each named executive
officer, other than Messrs.&nbsp;Helwig, Montgomery and Daily, the aggregate
dollar amount of perquisites or other personal benefits did not exceed the
lesser of (a)&nbsp;$50,000 or (b)&nbsp;10% of the total salary and bonus
reported by such named executive officer for such fiscal year. Certain of the
named executive officers receive a car allowance as a perquisite.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(2)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>In 2005, includes
amounts paid under the Company&#146;s Annual Incentive Compensation Program (&#147;AICP&#148;),
and payment of 25% of the signing bonuses described below ($75,000, $37,500,
$37,500 and $41,250 for Messrs.&nbsp;Helwig, Montgomery, Daily and Reiten,
respectively). In 2004, includes amounts paid under the AICP and vacation
bonuses for Mr.&nbsp;Helwig and Mr.&nbsp;Montgomery. In 2003, includes amounts
paid under the AICP and payment of 75% of the signing bonuses received in
connection with the merger transaction in which InfraSource Incorporated and
certain of its subsidiaries were acquired by InfraSource Services,&nbsp;Inc.
from Exelon Corporation (the &#147;Merger&#148;) as set forth in each named executive
officer&#146;s employment agreement ($225,000, $112,500, $112,500 and $123,750 for Messrs.&nbsp;Helwig,
Montgomery, Daily and Reiten, respectively). In 2003, amounts for Mr.&nbsp;Montgomery
also include an additional cash bonus of $35,000 and for Mr.&nbsp;Reiten a
retention payment of $125,000.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Seventy-five percent of
the signing bonus for each officer was paid in cash or shares of our common
stock, as elected by the officer, in 2003, and the remaining 25% of the signing
bonus was paid in September&nbsp;2005. For those officers who elected to have a
portion of their signing bonus paid in shares, we reimbursed them in respect of
the taxes incurred on the initial signing bonus shares and as well as any taxes
on the tax reimbursement, in accordance with the employment agreement terms.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition, each officer
is entitled to participate in our Annual Incentive Compensation Program and has
been granted options to purchase shares of our common stock.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In the event the officer&#146;s
employment is terminated by us for cause or terminated by the officer without
good reason, he will be entitled to receive his accrued base salary and
benefits through the termination date. In the event the officer&#146;s employment is
terminated as a result of the officer&#146;s death or disability, the officer or his
estate will be entitled to receive his accrued base salary and benefits through
the date of termination and any prorated share (based on the period of actual
employment) of any bonus under the Annual Incentive Compensation Program that
the officer would have been entitled to had he worked the full year during
which the termination occurred.</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">114</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In the event the officer&#146;s
employment is terminated following September&nbsp;24, 2005 by the officer for
good reason or by us for any reason other than the officer&#146;s death or
disability or for cause, in exchange for a release as to any and all claims,
the officer may have against us and an agreement not to compete until the
second anniversary of the date of his employment termination, the officer will
be entitled to the following severance benefits: (1)&nbsp;an amount equal to
the prorated share of his bonus under the Annual Incentive Compensation
Program, (2)&nbsp;an amount equal to two times the sum of his base salary at
the time of termination and (3)&nbsp;medical and health insurance benefits for
up to twenty-four months.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Each of the officers&#146;
employment agreements contains confidentiality, non-competition and
non-solicitation provisions effective through the term of the agreement and for
a period of two years thereafter if the officer is entitled to severance
benefits described above. Following the anniversary of the termination date, we
may elect to extend the non-competition period for an additional year by (1)&nbsp;paying
the officer the difference between his base salary at the time of his
termination and the option spread value of his vested shares at the time of his
termination and (2)&nbsp;providing health and insurance coverage for up to an
additional year. In the event the officer&#146;s employment is terminated following September&nbsp;24,
2005, by the officer without good reason, we may elect to extend the
non-competition period for up to two years by (1)&nbsp;paying the officer the
difference between two times his base salary at the time his termination and
the option spread value of the vested shares at the time of his termination and
(2)&nbsp;providing health and insurance coverage for up to an additional two
years.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In connection with the
Merger, Terence R. Montgomery and InfraSource Incorporated entered into a
Settlement Agreement and General Release of Claims. Under the agreement,
InfraSource Incorporated agreed to make a change of control payment to Mr.&nbsp;Montgomery
in the amount of $657,621, and Mr.&nbsp;Montgomery agreed to release any and
all claims under his employment agreement with InfraSource Incorporated.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On January&nbsp;27, 2004, Mr.&nbsp;Daily
entered into an amendment to cancel 25,419&nbsp;shares of the shares underlying
his September&nbsp;23, 2003 time-based stock option grant. Mr.&nbsp;Daily did
not receive any consideration for this cancellation of shares. All of the
cancelled shares were reallocated to other employees of InfraSource Underground
Services,&nbsp;Inc.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="OurIncentiveCompensationPlan_073111"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our
Incentive Compensation Plan</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Compensation Committee
has established an incentive compensation plan, which provides a framework for determining
corporate and individual goals for all executive officers and creates a pool of
potential bonus compensation for employees based upon the Company&#146;s achievement
of revenue and profit measures.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="CompensationOfDirectors_073113"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Compensation of
Directors</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We currently pay our non-employee
directors an annual retainer of $25,000 as fees related to their service on our
Board of Directors. Any non-employee director who also serves as Chairman of
the Board receives an annual retainer of $75,000 in lieu of the foregoing
retainer of $25,000. In addition, each non-employee director, including any who
also serve as Chairman of the Board, receives an additional annual retainer of
$5,000 for each committee on which he serves as a member, except that each
member of the Audit Committee receives an annual retainer of $7,500 for service
on the Audit Committee. In addition, the Chairman of the Audit Committee and
the Chairman of the Compensation Committee each receive an additional annual
retainer of $2,500 for their service as Chairman of each such committee. We
also reimburse all directors for reasonable expenses incurred to attend
meetings of our Board of Directors or committees.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 7.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition, each of our
non-employee directors elected to the Board of Directors for the first time is eligible
to receive, upon such election, an initial grant of stock options to purchase
19,913 shares of our commons stock at the fair market value of our common stock
on the date of grant. A non-employee </font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 3.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="CompensationCommitteeInterlocksAn_073116"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Compensation
Committee Interlocks and Insider Participation</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Mr.&nbsp;Brothers and Mr.&nbsp;Helwig
each served as officers of our company in 2003. Mr.&nbsp;Helwig currently
serves as our president and chief executive officer, and Mr.&nbsp;Brothers
resigned as an officer in October&nbsp;2003. Mr.&nbsp;Brothers was not an
officer or employee of our company during 2005. We do not expect that any of
our executive officers will serve as a director or member of the compensation
committee of another entity, one of whose executive officers serves on our
board of directors or compensation committee.</font></p>

and share price information is provided as of December&nbsp;31, 2005.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(2)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>The
number in Column (a)&nbsp;excludes purchase rights accruing under our
stockholder-approved employee stock purchase plan, the 2004 Employee Stock
Purchase Plan. This plan gives employees the right to purchase shares at
amounts and prices that are not determinable until the end of the specified
purchase periods, which occur at semi-annual intervals each year. The maximum
aggregate number of shares reserved for issuance under the plan is 2,000,000,
plus an annual increase to be added on the first day of our fiscal year
(beginning 2005) equal to the lesser of (i)&nbsp;600,000&nbsp;shares or
(ii)&nbsp;one percent of the number of our outstanding shares on the last day
of the immediately preceding fiscal year. As of January&nbsp;1, 2005, the
number of shares reserved for issuance under the plan was 2,389,427. From the
inception of the 2004 Employee Stock Purchase Plan through December,&nbsp;31,
2005, 183,321&nbsp;shares have been issued.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(3)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>The
maximum aggregate number of shares reserved for issuance under our 2004 Omnibus
Stock Incentive Plan is 800,000, plus an annual increase, to be added on the
first day of our fiscal year (beginning 2005) equal to the lesser of
(i)&nbsp;1,000,000 shares or (ii)&nbsp;two percent of our outstanding shares on
the last day of the immediately preceding fiscal year. As of January&nbsp;1,
2005, the aggregate number of shares reserved for issuance under the plan is
1,578,854&nbsp;shares. The term of the plan is ten years; therefore,
stockholder approval is not required for the automatic increase of shares.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 47.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-47.0pt;"><a name="Item13_CertainRelationshipsAndRel_070841"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Item
13.</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>CERTAIN
RELATIONSHIPS AND RELATED TRANSACTIONS</p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="ItsAcquisition_070843"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ITS Acquisition</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 11.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On January&nbsp;27, 2004,
InfraSource Services acquired all of the voting interests of Maslonka&nbsp;&amp;
Associates,&nbsp;Inc., now known as InfraSource Transmission Services Company (&#147;ITS&#148;),
for a total purchase price of $83.2 million, which included the issuance of
4,330,820 shares of InfraSource Services&#146; common stock, transaction costs and
purchase price contingencies. The value of the shares issued to Maslonka stockholders
was determined to be approximately $50.7 million. Martin Maslonka, a principal
stockholder of InfraSource Services, received $9.5 million in cash and
2,407,235 shares of InfraSource Services common stock. The final purchase price
was subject to a working capital adjustment and settlement of holdback
adjustments to the purchase price in accordance with the terms of the
acquisition agreement. Under the terms of the holdback provisions, InfraSource
Services withheld $6.6 million in cash payable at closing and 957,549 shares of
common stock, including $5.9 million in cash and 532,206 shares relating to Mr.&nbsp;Maslonka.
We finalized the working capital adjustment in July&nbsp;2005 and released $3.3
million in cash and 478,775 shares of common stock to the sellers in accordance
with the agreement, including $3.1 million in cash and 41,889 shares of common
stock to Mr.&nbsp;Maslonka. The balance of the holdback was released in January&nbsp;2006.<a name="ItsPerformanceBond_070845"></a></font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">119</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="ItsLease_070847"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ITS Lease</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 11.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We lease our ITS
headquarters in Mesa, Arizona and our ITS Texas field office in San Angelo,
Texas from EC Source, LLC, which is wholly owned by Martin Maslonka. Our leases
for these two properties will run through February&nbsp;2009, subject to a
five-year renewal option. Pursuant to these leases, we will incur total annual
lease payments of $0.2 million.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="ItsPromissoryNote_070848"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ITS Promissory Note</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 11.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ITS was the issuer of a
$1.0 million installment promissory note in favor of Martin Maslonka. The
promissory note had an annual interest rate of 8.5%, and interest is payable in
equal monthly payments of $7,083. The promissory note which was scheduled to
mature on June&nbsp;30, 2006 was repaid in December&nbsp;2005.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="BlairParkLiabilities_070849"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Blair Park Liabilities</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 11.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31,
2005, we had $7.1 million due to the former owners of Blair Park Services,&nbsp;Inc.
and Sunesys,&nbsp;Inc. (collectively &#147;Blair Park&#148;) accrued in other liabilities&#151;related
parties on our consolidated balance sheet for additional contingent purchase
price consideration. We acquired Blair Park in 2001.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="RegistrationRightsAgreement_070850"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Registration
Rights Agreement</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 11.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In January&nbsp;2004, we
entered into a registration rights agreement with our principal stockholders,
certain of our executive officers and the sellers in the ITS acquisition
transaction. Subject to certain conditions, the registration rights agreement
requires us to register the shares of InfraSource Services owned by such
stockholders with the SEC so that those shares may be publicly resold or to
include their shares in certain registration statements we file. Our principal
stockholders are entitled to require us to file a registration statement with
the SEC for the resale of their shares. The sellers in the ITS acquisition and
our executive officers are not entitled to require us to file a registration
statement but may include their shares in certain registration statements filed
by us. The underwriters of any underwritten offering will have the right to
limit the number of shares to be included in the filed registration statement. In
addition, we will pay all expenses (other than underwriting discounts and
commissions) on behalf of any selling stockholder participating in a registered
offering pursuant to the registration rights agreement.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 11.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:normal;">In December&nbsp;2005,
we amended the Registration Rights Agreement to add Tontine Capital Partners,
L.P. as a stockholder entitled to benefits under the agreement in connection
with the sale of shares of our common stock by our principal stockholders and
Martin Maslonka to Tontine Capital Partners, L.P.</font></b></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="ColemanPropertiesLease_073131"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Coleman Properties
Lease</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:6.0pt 0pt 11.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We lease office and warehouse space from Coleman Properties of which
Lawrence Coleman, President of Blair Park Services,&nbsp;Inc. and Sunesys,&nbsp;Inc.,
and his brothers are general partners. The lease for this space was to run
through October&nbsp;2005, subject to a 6 year renewal option. The terms of the
lease provided for an increase in rental payments equal to the increase in the
Consumer Price Index. In October,&nbsp;2005 we renewed the lease for three
years and our annual payments under this agreement are approximately $86,000. We
also lease ducts in two river bores under the Delaware River from Coleman
Properties. Our lease commenced on May&nbsp;1, 2005 and has a term of five
years, with an option to extend. Our annual lease payment is $0.02 million for
each pair of fiber installed in the conduit up to a maximum of $0.2 million per
year if additional ducts are leased.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 5.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><a name="StockholdersAgreement_073118"></a><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Stockholders&#146;
Agreement</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 11.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In September&nbsp;2003, we
and certain holders of our common stock became parties to a stockholders&#146;
agreement. Upon closing of the January&nbsp;2004 ITS transaction, the Maslonka sellers
were added as parties. This stockholders&#146; agreement gave our principal
stockholders a right of first refusal if any existing stockholder proposed to
transfer its common stock. Upon the closing of our initial public offering,
most of the provisions of the stockholders&#146; agreement, including those
providing for the right of first refusal, automatically terminated.</font></p>

to our registration statement for the initial public offering.</p>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Audit Committee&#146;s
Audit and Non-Audit Services Pre-Approval Policy (the &#147;Pre-Approval Policy&#148;)
provides for the pre-approval of audit and non-audit services performed by our
independent registered public accountant. Under the policy, the Audit Committee
may pre-approve specific services, including fee levels, by the independent
registered public accountant in a designated category (audit, audit-related,
tax services and all other services). The Audit Committee may delegate, in
writing, this authority to one or more of its members, provided that the member
or members to whom such authority is delegated must report their decisions to
the Audit Committee at its next scheduled meeting. As of the date of our
initial public offering, the Audit Committee adopted the Pre-Approval Policy.
All audit, audit-related and tax services provided to us by
PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP under engagements arising after the completion of
our initial public offering and before December&nbsp;31, 2005 have been
pre-approved by the Audit Committee.</font></p>
